proposal.title: Kalseful: an automated checker for accessible forms
proposal.summary: Kalseful builds an automated checker for accessible forms for people who rely on assistive technology.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Public forms are often unusable with a screen reader. People who rely on assistive technology are depending from web accessibility every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build an automated checker for accessible forms called Kalseful. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Web accessibility belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/kalseful/kalseful, which 277 public projects depend on. Our team is working on web accessibility for 10 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/kalseful/kalseful. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 48700.00 EUR for 101 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 500.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Public forms are often unusable with a screen reader. People who rely on assistive technology are depending from web accessibility every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build an automated checker for accessible forms called Kalseful. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Web accessibility belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/kalseful/kalseful, which 277 public projects depend on. Our team is working on web accessibility for 10 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under MIT licence in http://forge.test/kalseful/kalseful. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 48700.00 EUR for 101 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 500.00 EUR.
